weights_gb_note: decimal GB; bf16 = 2 x params (= sum of the HF-format safetensors shards); 4bit = NF4 + double-quant estimate (0.5159 B per quantisable decoder-layer linear weight, rest in bf16)
fits_single_80gb_detail: bf16: 64.5 GB weights (60.1 GiB); sbx.core.Ctx.hidden_last needs 0.83 MiB per prompt token (hidden states of all 64 layers + full logits; no KV cache is built because the config has use_cache=false): at most ~22.8k padded tokens per chunk next to the weights (estimate), enough for the current direction pools (prompts are capped at 7500 characters by sbx/evals.py) but a single raw 26k-token LabBench CloningScenarios prompt (~21 GiB vs 18.4 GiB free after weights and a 0.8 GiB CUDA context) would OOM (hidden_last_80gb)

hidden_last_80gb.verdict: fits: no hidden_last chunk of the hard / wmdp / nonbio direction pools exceeds the free memory of an 80 GB card (a prompt above max_tokens_per_chunk tokens would).
hidden_last_80gb.basis: ESTIMATE from config numbers, not a GPU measurement. sbx.core.Ctx.hidden_last / neutral_stats call model(**enc, output_hidden_states=True): per prompt token the hidden states of all layers ((num_layers+1) * hidden_size * 2 B), the full-sequence logits (vocab_size * 2 B) and, only if the model config has use_cache=true (forward(use_cache=None) then builds a cache; kv_cache_alive says so, and all OLMo configs ship use_cache=false), the KV cache (2 * layers * kv_heads * head_dim * 2 B; an upper bound for sliding-window layers) are alive at once, and bytes_per_prompt_token is their sum. core.batches() budgets KV, prefill attention and a 14000-token chunk but not this cost. free_gib_after_weights = 79.2 GiB (an 80 GB card) - 0.8 GiB (CUDA context) - bf16 weights. max_tokens_per_chunk = free / bytes_per_prompt_token: a chunk of b prompts padded to length p holds b*p tokens, and a single prompt above the limit cannot be processed at all. hard_pool_measured: core.batches(max_new=0, cap=16, free) over the direction-pool prompts evals.get_pool()['hard'] under framings N and E with this adapter and the real tokenizer; chunks_over_budget counts chunks whose estimated peak exceeds the free memory. Measured 2026-11-22; the pool follows sbx/evals.py (n_prompts and max_prompt_chars identify it).

access_check.method: HfApi.model_info + HTTP HEAD (huggingface_hub.get_hf_file_metadata) with the local HF token on config.json and the first safetensors shard (200 = accessible, 401/403 raise)

min_transformers_note: olmo3 first appears in the 4.57.0 wheel (absent in 4.56.2; checked); README says 'transformers 4.57.0 or higher'

layer_path_verified.method: AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(real hub config) under accelerate.init_empty_weights (meta device); numerics of the 1-based convention on a tiny random model of the same HF class through sbx.core.Ctx (sbx/tests/test_adapters_misc.py)
layer_path_verified.convention: hidden_states[L] == output of layers[L-1] for 1 <= L < nl (exact); hidden_states[nl] is post final norm (avoid L = nl)

checkpoint_key_check.method: keys of model.safetensors.index.json (after the class's _checkpoint_conversion_mapping) vs meta-device state_dict, transformers 4.57.6

est_prompt_tokens.basis: measured over data/questions_heldout_eval.jsonl (400 four-option bio questions) with the real tokenizer + adapter.build; long-context sets (labbench) are much longer

prompt_tokens_by_set.basis: framing N, real tokenizer + adapter.build over data/hard/*.jsonl, data/questions_heldout_eval.jsonl, data/wmdp_train.jsonl; n_over_context counts prompts with prompt_tokens + max_new > context_window

est_tokens_per_question_basis: estimate; NOT measured. Replace with the mean generated length from the first GPU run; outputs longer than max_new are truncated and count as unparsed.
template_notes: Previous 32B Think release; same format as olmo-3.1-32b-think (think block opened in the prompt, '</think>' is plain text) but its default system prompt is only 'You are a helpful AI assistant.'. Same boilerplate handling as olmo-3.1-32b-think: the template's default render has none while a given system message gets it appended, so N goes through an explicit system turn ('You are a helpful AI assistant. You do not currently have access to any functions. <functions></functions>': NOT the vendor's default render) and a framed prompt is exactly N plus the framing paragraph (tested for every key). Set the class attribute adapter.keep_default_system = False to get the vendor template's native semantics (framing REPLACES the default system prompt; N is unchanged).
known_issues: N is NOT the vendor's default render: it carries the template-appended '<functions></functions>' boilerplate (+14 tokens) so that N and every framed prompt differ only by the framing paragraph; absolute N accuracy can therefore differ slightly from numbers obtained with the bare vendor default render.

Vendor sampling: temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95. sbx decodes greedily; the vendor recommends sampling for this model, and greedy decoding of long-CoT models is prone to repetition loops -> look at the parse rate / truncation rate of baseline N before reading any steering effect.
Same architecture/tokenizer as olmo-3.1-32b-think (the 3.1 release continues RL training).
greedy_only_note: sbx decodes greedily; the vendor recommends sampling for this model, and greedy decoding of long-CoT models is prone to repetition loops -> look at the parse rate / truncation rate of baseline N before reading any steering effect.
